findings.reason: The protected SQL solution uses LEAD(visit_date) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY visit_date) in a CTE to attach each user's next visit date, uses COALESCE(next_visit, '2021-01-01') for terminal visits, computes day differences, and takes MAX per user_id AS biggest_window. The solution is canonical, optimal, and concise; no candidate is required.

LEAD partitioned by user_id and ordered by visit_date pairs each visit with the next chronological visit for that user. Replacing NULL next_visit values with 2021-01-01 correctly measures the terminal gap for the latest visit. MAX per user_id selects the largest gap.
Window ranking and grouping over R visit rows takes O(R) time using composite index order or O(R log R) time with general sorting, and O(R) space. Complexity evidence is certified and hash-bound.
Outputs columns user_id and biggest_window, correctly uses 2021-01-01 as default next visit for terminal visits, and handles single-visit users.

The approach accurately details LEAD windowing by user_id, replacing nulls with 2021-01-01, MAX grouping, and relational complexity bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover self-joins, correlated subqueries, global LEAD errors, unordered window bugs, single visits, terminal gap wins, unsorted rows, leap year date math, and result ordering flexibility.

App SQL and native SQL solutions both execute the exact same LEAD windowing, COALESCE 2021-01-01 terminal handling, and MAX grouping with SHA-256 digests 0db73566ccbd0b09d924bfd08a87a06efd434658525c63bb41a55a900982487e and 394d680ae1a3d1a0b3e01355036ae1640e13674bd57d6754a7582f8dde925647.
